# Check — M0-a-06, transactions: closing check of the kernel's consolidation round R6 (lane check/M0-a-06-consolidate-close-1, 2026-10-13)

**Verdict: PASS.** This checker re-ran every failing line of the round against its oracle and found each one fixed:
T-1; T-2, T-4 and T-5; T-3; T-6 – T-9 with §2's tx rows; T-tx; API frozen; NO-SHIFT. The evidence is this checker's
own. No new finding is a blocker. The round changes no behaviour:

* **Before-images.** The pre-round sources are the real ones, not reconstructions. They come from `main` at `b1d48323`
  through the GitHub contents API (`gh api`, raw; no git). The last commit of each owned file there is round S4 or S5
  of 10-08 / 10-11, so those files are the tree as R6 found it. Eight of the ten `src/tx` files differ from the tree;
  `ops.ts` and `types.ts` are byte-equal.
* **NO-SHIFT.** This checker's own probe covers 52 230 batches: fuzz.test.ts's registered families and regressions,
  plus widened default, along and heavy mixes. Per batch it records the record, refusal code and text, `bits(p)`, the
  print, records per level, chunk refs, level digests, `runsOfPairs` and `routeLines`. The output is byte-identical on
  the pre-round sources and the tree (sha256 `645cb597…`). The probe is sensitive: mutant C14 moves 8 009 lines.
* **Refusals.** The registered families' counts are the same before and after: default 59 / 336, along 104 / 384,
  regressions 49 / 220.
* **Exports.** These are identical: 422 runtime values in the barrel, 30 in `tx/index.ts`, and the barrel's emitted
  `index.d.ts`. The one type-level change is `runsOfPairs`, from a function declaration to a `const` of type
  `typeof edgeRuns`. Its signature is unchanged: `(p: Plat, pairsIn: readonly number[]) => HalfEdgeId[][]`.
* **Old and new tests.** The pre-round tests (17 files, smoke included) pass on the new sources: 28 runs, 444 / 444.
  The consolidated tests pass on the pre-round sources: 28 / 456, so T-tx-new-1 holds at 10⁴ on the OLD body. Every
  title is kept: 53 / 122 → 54 / 128, none missing.
* **Mutants.** 41 runs. Every earlier mutant the plan's oracles name, and which an earlier check killed, is red again.
  Every mutant aimed at this round's changes is red, except C10. C10 and the two non-blocking survivors (X12, X16c)
  survive the pre-round line too.

One pre-existing defect is routed to the session (N-c1-6, widening the author's N-c1-5). Some committed arenas of the
item's own families cannot be encoded, and on them `routeLines` throws: 14 sequences, one of them a registered
regression. The behaviour is identical before and after, and this round may not change behaviour, so it is not this
round's blocker. It is a fix round for M0-a-06 (N-45 (a)).

Seat: closing checker, independent of the author. The lane log had no line for this lane key, so the check started
fresh. This checker planned its probes and mutants before reading the author's round-C1 notes section. It read that
section, choices row C-0350 and CLEAN-ROOM row L-0493 afterwards, and judges them here rather than using them as
evidence. Machine id `linux:Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz:4cpu:16gib` (J198, matches); Node v24.12.0;
`test_budget.py` printed 1 worker and 1 mutant slot. No timing was taken or gated on. No git command was run.

## Method

* **Mirrors** under `scratchpad/waves/check-M0-a-06/`, each a whole copy of `plat/` with its own `node_modules`:
  * `after`: the tree. `diff -rq` against the tree is clean apart from this checker's `zz-*` probe files, which were
    removed after each use.
  * `pre`: `after` with the eight pre-round `src/tx` files from `main` swapped in. `tsc --noEmit` exits 0.

  A first `before` mirror, reconstructed from the plan's text, was used before the real sources were fetched. It
  instrumented the old rotation walk and was then replaced by `pre`. Each mutant was restored and `cmp`-checked
  against the tree, or against `main`'s file for `pre`.
* **Probes** (scratch only, never in the tree):
  * `zz-check-c1-golden.test.ts`, the NO-SHIFT golden.
  * `zz-check-c1-enc.test.ts`, which classifies the encoder refusals.
  * `zz-check-c1-open.test.ts`, the T-3 fail-safe.
  * `exports.mts`, the runtime export census.
  * `rng.mts`, the generator against a textbook mulberry32.

## (3) New findings, judged by the blocker rule

No blocker. Notes appended to `checks/M0-a-06-notes.md` under "Round C1 — the closing check's notes":

* **N-c1-6.** The pre-existing encoder refusal and `routeLines` throw (the author's N-c1-5) is wider than three
  sequences: 14, among them the registered regression 106 ×15 485 863. `healthy` passes it, and so does a whole-arena
  level scan. It is identical before and after. J290: OUR OWN INTERMEDIATE, MAKE-IT-SUCCEED, routed to the session for
  a fix round of M0-a-06 (M0, N-45 (a)), with the seeds.
* **N-c1-7.** C10: `enterWriter`'s limit boundary has no pin (pre-existing; M4).
* **N-c1-8.** C12 and N1: the tx clearance row's boundary has no unit pin (pre-existing; M4).
* **N-c1-9.** X16 / X16c survive, subsumed by `onStretch` (pre-existing; X16b is killed).
* **N-c1-10.** Two comment completions (C-tx-1's dropped "never a batch's substitute"; `op`'s value list).

The item checker's own line: no tie-break in `src/tx` reads a slot. `source.test.ts` is green, and its comparator-key
list now names `comparePoints`. Every new comparator in the diff reads lattice points.
